mainTopic: The disagreement of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע on whether blood needs meat, and whether our משנה of five public offerings brought in טומאה can follow רבי יהושע
overview: Background: רבי יהושע holds that a קרבן needs both its blood and its meat. רבי אליעזר holds that the blood is thrown even when there is no meat. First the גמרא explains how each of them reads the פסוק 'ועשית עלתיך הבשר והדם... ודם זבחיך ישפך... והבשר תאכל'. It also explains where each one learns that the meat may not be eaten until the blood is thrown: רבי אליעזר from the פסוק, and רבי יהושע from a קל וחומר. Then the גמרא asks whether our משנה can follow רבי יהושע. That משנה says five public offerings, such as the עומר and the שתי הלחם, may be brought in טומאה. One answer is that for רבי יהושע the ציץ fixes the parts burned on the מזבח and that his rule does not apply to מנחות. A ברייתא of רבי יוסי knocks this down. A second answer is that the ציץ also fixes the eaten parts. A משנה about מנחות and a ברייתא of רבי יהושע knock this down too. Finally the גמרא suggests that רבי יהושע is strict only לכתחילה, and it proves he makes that distinction. But the wording פסולה and חמשה דברים באין shows that this distinction cannot explain our משנה.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהושע need two verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק teaches the link between blood and meat twice, according to רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need these two verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that, for רבי יהושע, two parts of the פסוק seem to teach the same rule: blood and meat go together. It asks why both are needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ועשית עלתיך הבשר והדם' already links meat and blood. 'ודם זבחיך ישפך... והבשר תאכל' links them a second time. The תורה does not repeat itself for nothing, so the גמרא wants to know what the second source adds.

keyTerms.meaning: verses (plural of קְרָא)
why do I need it? A question about a source that seems extra
two

phrases.english: And these two verses
phrases.notes: The two parts of the פסוק that link blood with meat.

phrases.english: why do I need them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about how רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר read the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does each of the two sources teach that the other does not?

steps.title: One verse for עולה, one for שלמים
steps.stepSummary: Each verse teaches the rule for a different kind of קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about a burnt-offering, and one is about a peace-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two verses are not repeats. One teaches the rule for an עולה and the other teaches it for שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עלתיך' is about an עולה. 'זבחיך' is about שלמים. So each kind of קרבן gets its own source showing that the blood depends on the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
peace-offering, mostly eaten by the owners and the כהנים
one

phrases.english: One is about a burnt-offering,
and one is about a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verses split between עולה and שלמים, so neither one is extra.

steps.title: Why a verse about עולה alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If only עולה were written, we might think the rule applies only to a strict קרבן that is burned completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If the Merciful One had written it only about a burnt-offering, I would have said: it is the burnt-offering that is strict, since it is burned completely. But a peace-offering, which is not strict, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain why both verses are needed (a צריכותא). This step shows why the עולה verse alone would leave room for a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is כליל: all of it goes on the מזבח. That makes it more serious, so its meat might matter more. שלמים are mostly eaten by people, so we might have thought their meat is not needed before the blood is thrown.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is necessary: the opening of a צְרִיכוּתָא, showing that both sources are needed
the Merciful One, meaning the תורה
I would have said: a mistaken first thought
completely burned on the מזבח
strict or severe

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written it about a burnt-offering,
I would have said: it is the burnt-offering that is strict,
since it is burned completely,
but a peace-offering, which is not strict,
I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer in step 2 by showing that the עולה verse alone would not cover שלמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולה verse alone could not teach the rule for שלמים, because the strictness of an עולה is a reason that does not apply to שלמים.

steps.title: Why a verse about שלמים alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If only שלמים were written, we might think its meat matters more because it is eaten in two ways, so the תורה had to teach both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Merciful One had written it only about a peace-offering, I would have said: on the contrary, it has two eatings. But a burnt-offering, which does not have two eatings, I would say no. So the verse teaches us both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא from the other side. It shows that the שלמים verse alone would also leave room for a mistake, so both verses are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים have שתי אכילות: some parts burn on the מזבח, and people eat the rest. So their meat could seem more important than the meat of an עולה. Each קרבן has its own reason to stand out, so neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: on the contrary
two eatings: by the מזבח and by people
it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהושע, both parts of the פסוק are needed. Each kind of קרבן has its own special feature (an עולה is כליל, שלמים have שתי אכילות), so we cannot learn one from the other.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written it about a peace-offering,
I would have said: on the contrary,
since it has two eatings.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹלָה דְּלֵית בָּהּ שְׁתֵּי אֲכִילוֹת,
phrases.english: But a burnt-offering, which does not have two eatings,
I would say no,
so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא שְׁלָמִים, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both verses are needed for רבי יהושע: one for עולה and one for שלמים.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי אליעזר also has 'והבשר תאכל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר: the same פסוק ends with 'והבשר תאכל', which seems to tie the blood to the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי אליעזר too, isn't it written: 'And the meat you shall eat'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי אליעזר. He reads 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' as saying the blood is thrown even with no meat. But the words 'והבשר תאכל' come right after the blood, which seems to link them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע learns from these words that blood needs meat for שלמים. So the challenge is: how can רבי אליעזר ignore the connection that the פסוק itself makes?

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it written? A challenge from a פסוק
'and the meat you shall eat' (דברים יב:כז)
also, too

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Eliezer too,
isn't it written: 'And the meat you shall eat'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining רבי יהושע's sources to challenging רבי אליעזר's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that the blood is thrown even when there is no meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק puts meat right next to blood, which suggests they depend on each other. That goes against רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the phrase teaches that meat waits for the blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses 'והבשר תאכל' for a different rule: the meat may not be eaten until the blood is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: that phrase is needed to teach that the meat is not permitted to be eaten until the blood is thrown.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the challenge. He says the words 'והבשר תאכל' teach a different lesson, so they do not support רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the פסוק, blood first and then 'eat the meat', teaches the order of actions. Eating comes only after זריקת הדם. So the link is one-way: the meat depends on the blood, but the blood does not depend on the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: he would say to you: an answer given on someone's behalf
he needs it for something else
until the blood is thrown on the מזבח (זְרִיקָה)

phrases.english: He would say to you:
that phrase is needed by him
to teach that the meat is not permitted to be eaten
until the blood is thrown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the source: the phrase is used for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'והבשר תאכל' makes the blood depend on the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והבשר תאכל' only makes eating the meat depend on throwing the blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that meat of a קרבן may not be eaten before זריקת הדם is a basic rule of קדשים.

steps.title: Then where is רבי אליעזר's own source?
steps.stepSummary: If the whole פסוק is about meat waiting for the blood, then רבי אליעזר seems to have no source for throwing blood without meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, say that the whole verse comes for this purpose! Then where do we learn that blood is thrown even when there is no meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the פסוק is teaching the order of blood and then meat, maybe all of it, including 'ודם זבחיך ישפך', is part of that one lesson. Then רבי אליעזר has no source for his rule. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's proof came from reading 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' as a separate statement about blood. But if that phrase is just the first half of 'throw the blood, then eat the meat', it no longer teaches anything on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
all of it, the whole verse
from where do we learn it?
even though

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the rule that meat waits for the blood. It is a challenge to רבי אליעזר's own source: once the פסוק is used for that rule, nothing seems left to teach that blood is thrown without meat.

phrases.english: If so,
say that the whole verse comes for this purpose!

phrases.aramaic: דָּם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין שָׁם בָּשָׂר
phrases.english: That blood is thrown even though there is no meat
from where do we learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא כּוּלֵּיהּ לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6 by showing that it removes רבי אליעזר's own proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's source for throwing blood even without meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק is one teaching about the order of blood and meat, 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' cannot also stand alone as the source for throwing blood when there is no meat.

steps.title: The word order of the verse teaches two rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the פסוק put the blood before the meat on purpose, so it teaches both 'blood alone works' and 'meat waits for blood.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר can tell you: If the פסוק only meant that the meat waits for the blood, the תורה should have written 'eat the meat' first and then 'the blood shall be poured,' the same order used at the start of the פסוק ('your עולות, the meat and the blood'). Why did it put 'the blood of your offerings' first? Learn two things from this: blood works even when there is no meat, and the meat may not be eaten until the blood is thrown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. רבי אליעזר shows that the odd order of the words in the פסוק gives him a source for both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning of the פסוק lists meat before blood, but the end of the פסוק lists blood before meat. This change in order is a hint. The blood standing alone at the front teaches that blood counts even without meat. The connection to 'והבשר תאכל' teaches that the meat waits for the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading were correct)
The Merciful One (the תורה)
At the beginning (of the פסוק)
What is different? Why the change?
It put it first
Learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, one פסוק teaches two rules because of its word order: (1) blood can be thrown even without meat, and (2) meat may not be eaten until the blood is thrown.

phrases.english: He [רבי אליעזר] could say to you: If so,
the Merciful One should have written "the meat you shall eat"
and afterward "and the blood of your offerings shall be poured out,"
just as it is written at the beginning [of the verse]
"And you shall offer your burnt-offerings, the meat and the blood,"
phrases.notes: Here meat comes first and blood second.

phrases.english: What is different that it put "the blood of your offerings" first?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: דָּם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: Learn from it: blood [is thrown] even though there is no meat,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: שֶׁאֵין הַבָּשָׂר מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה
phrases.english: and learn from it: that the meat is not permitted to be eaten
until the blood is thrown.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7's challenge that רבי אליעזר had no source left for throwing blood without meat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual anomaly (unusual word order) yields a double derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole end of the פסוק teaches only that the meat waits for the blood, so רבי אליעזר has no source for blood without meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because blood is placed first, against the order at the start of the פסוק, the verse teaches both rules.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהושע learn that meat waits for the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי יהושע's source for the rule that meat may not be eaten before the blood is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע: from where does he learn that the meat may not be eaten until the blood is thrown?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יהושע. He uses 'והבשר תאכל' to tie the blood to the meat, so the גמרא asks where he learns that the meat waits for the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר used the end of the פסוק for the rule that meat waits for blood. רבי יהושע already used that phrase for his own rule, that blood needs meat. So he must have another source, and this question sets up the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to be eaten
That it is thrown (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua:
[from where does he know that] the meat is not permitted to be eaten
until the blood is thrown?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, אֵין הַבָּשָׂר מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה עַד שֶׁיִּזָּרֵק הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing רבי אליעזר's sources, the גמרא checks whether רבי יהושע has a source for the second rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהושע's source for the rule that meat may not be eaten before the blood is thrown.

steps.title: רבי יהושע learns it from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע derives the rule through a קל וחומר from the אימורים: if they hold back the eating, blood surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר. The אימורים do not hold back the קרבן when they are missing, yet when they are present they hold back the eating until they are burned. Blood holds back the קרבן even when it is missing. So when it is present, surely it holds back the eating until it is thrown!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע needs no פסוק, because he can learn this rule through a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אימורים are lost, the קרבן is still valid. But if they exist, the meat waits until they are offered. Blood is more important: if it is lost, the קרבן fails. So when the blood exists, the meat surely must wait for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
The fat parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
They hold back or prevent
When they are not present
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: 'מעכב' is used in two senses here. When a part is missing, it means 'its absence ruins the קרבן.' When a part is present, it means 'it holds back the eating until it is offered.'

phrases.english: It is a kal vachomer:
Just as the sacrificial fats, which when they are not present
do not hold back [the offering],
yet when they are present, they do hold back [the eating];
blood, which when it is not present does hold back [the offering],
when it is present,
is it not all the more so that it holds back [the eating]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the אימורים to the blood.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר needs a verse for something logic teaches
steps.stepSummary: If a קל וחומר teaches the rule, why does רבי אליעזר use a פסוק? Because the תורה sometimes writes a rule even when logic could teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, why does he need a פסוק if there is a קל וחומר? Sometimes a matter that could be learned through a קל וחומר is still written out by the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר takes the rule from a פסוק if a קל וחומר already teaches it. It answers that the תורה sometimes takes the trouble to write such a rule anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that a פסוק should not be 'used up' on a rule that logic already gives. רבי אליעזר answers that this does happen: the תורה sometimes writes a rule outright even when a קל וחומר could teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter or rule
Took the trouble
A פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer? [Why does he need a verse?]
A matter that comes from a kal vachomer,
the verse took the trouble and wrote it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהושע's קל וחומר from Step 10 to challenge רבי אליעזר's use of the פסוק in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's use of the פסוק for 'meat waits for blood'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule available through a קל וחומר should not need a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסוק is never spent on a rule that a קל וחומר teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה sometimes writes out a rule that could be learned through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: expound the verse for something new
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע holds that whenever a פסוק can teach something new, we read it that way, so 'והבשר תאכל' teaches that blood needs meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע, why does he not accept that? Wherever there is something new to learn from the פסוק, we learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהושע disagrees with that principle. He holds that if a פסוק can teach a new rule, we use it for that new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, the rule that meat waits for the blood already comes from the קל וחומר. So he uses the פסוק for something new: that the blood depends on the meat. This is the root of the disagreement between the two תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Anywhere, wherever
To expound (a פסוק)
We expound

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the תורה may write out a rule that logic teaches, so his פסוק teaches both rules. רבי יהושע: a פסוק should teach something new, so it teaches that blood needs meat, and the meat waiting for blood comes from the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua? [How does he respond?]
Anywhere that there is something to expound,
we expound.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ? כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא לְמִדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהושע's response to the principle stated for רבי אליעזר in Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע might accept that the פסוק repeats what the קל וחומר teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע expounds the פסוק for a new rule, that blood depends on meat.

steps.title: Does our משנה contradict רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests our משנה cannot follow רבי יהושע. He needs both blood and meat, and the ציץ does not fix טומאה of eaten parts, so how could the five public offerings in our משנה be brought in טומאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, let us say our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע. He said we need both the blood and the meat, and the ציץ does not make up for טומאה of the parts that are eaten. So how can these offerings be brought in טומאה?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the background just built, the גמרא suggests that our משנה, which lets five public offerings (עומר, שתי הלחם, לחם הפנים, שלמי ציבור, שעירי ראש חודש) be brought in טומאה, does not fit רבי יהושע. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע requires the meat for the blood to be thrown. If the meat is טמא, and the ציץ does not fix טומאה of eaten parts, the meat does not count. Then the blood should not be thrown, so public offerings brought in טומאה should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Now
Let us say (a suggestion to be tested)
The כהן גדול's golden frontplate, which makes up for certain טומאה
Makes the קרבן acceptable
The parts of a קרבן that are eaten
Ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' is a suggestion, not a final ruling. The גמרא is testing whether the משנה really goes against רבי יהושע, and it may still find a way to fit them together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the long מחלוקת back to our משנה about the five public offerings brought in טומאה. It shows why the sources were worked out in such detail.

phrases.english: Now, let us say that our Mishnah
is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua,
since he said that we need both [meat and blood],
and the frontplate does not make the eaten parts acceptable,
how can it be brought in impurity?

steps.title: The frontplate fixes the impurity of the parts burned on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow רבי יהושע after all, because he holds the ציץ atones for the טומאה of the parts that go up on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows רבי יהושע, there is no problem. רבי יהושע holds that the ציץ fixes the impurity of the parts that are burned on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question. It shows that our משנה can still follow רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע needs something besides the blood to be valid. The ציץ does not fix impure meat that is eaten, but it does fix impure אימורים that are burned on the מזבח. So when the offering is brought in טומאה, the burned parts still count as the second valid part, and the blood may be thrown.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (you can still hold it follows this view)

steps.terutzMaskana: The burned parts are made valid by the ציץ, so the requirement of two parts is met.

steps.title: What about the עומר and the שתי הלחם, which have no burned parts?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for animal offerings, but the עומר and שתי הלחם have nothing extra burned on the מזבח, so how can they come in טומאה under רבי יהושע?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for animal offerings, which have parts that go up on the מזבח. But the עומר and the שתי הלחם have no such parts. What can you say about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It points to offerings in our משנה where that answer does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists the עומר and שתי הלחם among the offerings that may come in טומאה. In a מנחה, the קומץ (handful) plays the role of the blood, and the rest is eaten. Since nothing else goes on the מזבח, the ציץ has no burned parts to fix, so there is no valid second part.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's rule applies only to animal offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע required both parts only for זבחים, not for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: when רבי יהושע said we need both parts, he said it about animal offerings. About מנחות he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the עומר and שתי הלחם. It limits רבי יהושע's rule to animal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a מנחה, רבי יהושע does not require the remaining part to be valid. So the קומץ can be offered even if the rest is impure. That is why the עומר and שתי הלחם can come in טומאה, even under רבי יהושע.

steps.terutzMaskana: His rule applies only to זבחים, so מנחות like the עומר can come in טומאה.

steps.title: A משנה applies רבי יהושע's rule to meal-offerings
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if the rest of a מנחה became impure or was lost, it is פסולה according to רבי יהושע's view, so he does seem to apply his rule to מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he really not say it about מנחות? But we learned in a משנה: if the rest of the מנחה became impure or was lost, by רבי אליעזר's principle it is valid, but by רבי יהושע's principle it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer with a משנה. That משנה seems to show רבי יהושע's rule does apply to מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said רבי יהושע's rule is only for animal offerings. But this משנה invalidates a מנחה whose remainder is impure or lost, "according to רבי יהושע." That means his need for two parts does apply to מנחות.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה invalidates a מנחה with a lost or impure remainder according to רבי יהושע, showing he needs both parts even in מנחות.

steps.title: That תנא follows רבי יהושע's principle but extends it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהושע's principle of needing two parts, but goes further than רבי יהושע himself by applying it to מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is "like his principle" and "not like his principle." It is like רבי יהושע in that we need two parts. It is not like רבי יהושע, because he said it only about animal offerings, while this תנא holds it applies even to מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the משנה. It explains that the משנה uses רבי יהושע's idea but stretches it further than he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כמדת רבי יהושע mean "following his method," not "quoting his exact ruling." This תנא takes רבי יהושע's idea of needing both parts and applies it to מנחות. רבי יהושע himself limited it to זבחים, so the answer of Step 16 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his principle, and yet not like his principle (partly follows it)

steps.confusionAlert: כמדת רבי יהושע does not mean "this is רבי יהושע's ruling." It means "using רבי יהושע's way of thinking," which a later תנא can apply more widely than רבי יהושע did.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a principle can be named after a תנא even when another תנא applies it in places the original תנא did not.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה's phrase כמדת as "following the principle" and attributes the extension to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה reports רבי יהושע's own ruling about מנחות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's תנא extends רבי יהושע's principle to מנחות. רבי יהושע himself applied it only to זבחים.

steps.title: Who is this stricter Tanna?

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 18. That answer claimed the משנה follows an unnamed תנא who is stricter than רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 invented a third view: someone who takes רבי יהושע's 'both parts needed' rule and applies it to מנחות, even though רבי יהושע himself did not. The גמרא asks who this person is. Inventing an unknown תנא just to save the answer is weak.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Both views apply to animal offerings and to meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge. רבי יוסי says the words of both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע apply to זבחים and to מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי said: I see as correct the words of רבי אליעזר about מנחות and זבחים, and the words of רבי יהושע about זבחים and מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step is the heading, and the next step explains it in detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said רבי יהושע required both parts only for זבחים. Here רבי יוסי states that רבי יהושע's view covers מנחות too. If that is true, Step 16 and Step 18 both fall apart.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records רבי יהושע's view as applying to מנחות as well.

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי spells out each view. רבי יהושע requires both parts in זבחים (blood and meat) and also in מנחות (קומץ and שיריים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר's view on זבחים: the blood works even if there is no meat. רבי יהושע's view on זבחים: no blood means no meat, and no meat means no blood. רבי אליעזר's view on מנחות: the קומץ works even if there are no שיריים. רבי יהושע's view on מנחות: no קומץ means no שיריים, and no שיריים means no קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains exactly what each sage holds. This proves that רבי יהושע applies his two-part rule to מנחות too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'if there are no שיריים, there is no קומץ' is רבי יהושע's own rule for מנחות. So he does not limit his rule to זבחים. Steps 16 and 18 are now disproven, and the question from Step 15 about the עומר and שתי הלחם comes back.

steps.title: The frontplate atones even for the eaten portions
steps.stepSummary: A new answer. רבי יהושע holds that the ציץ atones for impurity of the parts burned on the מזבח and also of the parts that are eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהושע holds that the ציץ atones both for the parts that go up on the מזבח and for the parts that are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier approach and gives a new answer. It changes what רבי יהושע holds about the ציץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 14) we assumed that for רבי יהושע, the ציץ helps only for the parts that go up on the מזבח. Impure meat or impure שיריים therefore counted as 'missing.' Now the ציץ also covers the eaten parts, so impure meat or impure שיריים still count as present. Both parts exist, and the עומר and שתי הלחם can be brought in טומאה even according to רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the previous approach)
He holds
The כהן גדול's golden frontplate brings acceptance (for impurity)
The parts that go up on the מזבח
The parts that are eaten

steps.whatToRemember: New proposal: according to רבי יהושע, the ציץ covers impurity of both the burned parts and the eaten parts. If so, טומאה would not count as 'missing' a part, and the משנה about public offerings brought in טומאה would fit רבי יהושע. The גמרא tests this in Steps 23–26 and rejects it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the line of argument. The question is no longer whether רבי יהושע's two-part rule applies to מנחות. Instead, טומאה never breaks the two-part rule, because the ציץ fixes it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
the frontplate appeases
for [the parts that go up and for] the parts that are eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Steps 19–21 and replaces the approach of Steps 14–18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the earlier assumption about how far the ציץ's atonement reaches according to רבי יהושע
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי יהושע, the ציץ atones only for impurity of the burned parts, so impure eaten parts count as missing
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהושע, the ציץ atones for impurity of the eaten parts too, so they count as present and the offering is valid

steps.title: Then why is the meal offering disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: If the ציץ covers the eaten parts, why does the משנה say an impure מנחה is פסולה according to רבי יהושע?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה say that according to רבי יהושע's principle it is פסולה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer from Step 22, using the משנה quoted in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in Step 17 said that if the שיריים became impure or were lost, the מנחה is פסולה according to רבי יהושע's principle. If the ציץ fixes impurity of eaten parts, impure שיריים should still count as present. So why would it be פסולה?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ציץ atones for impurity of eaten parts according to רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that a מנחה with impure שיריים is פסולה according to רבי יהושע. That ruling only makes sense if the ציץ does not fix impurity of eaten parts.

steps.title: Only when lost or burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's ruling of פסולה refers only to שיריים that were lost or burned, not to שיריים that became impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling refers to the cases where the rest was lost or burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'פסולה' applies only to the cases where the rest no longer exists at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שיריים are lost or burned, they are truly gone, and nothing can fix that. So according to רבי יהושע the קומץ fails too. If they only became impure, the ציץ fixes it, and the מנחה stays valid. The answer from Step 22 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Lost
Burned

phrases.english: It refers to the cases of lost and burned.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the משנה's ruling applies only to some of its cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'פסולה' covers impure, lost, and burned שיריים alike
steps.terutzMaskana: 'פסולה' according to רבי יהושע applies only to lost or burned שיריים. Impure שיריים are covered by the ציץ.

steps.title: The impure case in the משנה must belong to רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects step 24's answer. The case of נטמא in the משנה is pointless for רבי אליעזר, so it must be teaching רבי יהושע's view, and it says פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then whose view does the case of "became impure" teach? For רבי אליעזר it is obvious. He already says the offering is valid when the leftovers were lost or burned and no longer exist at all. Do we even need to say it is valid when they became impure and still exist? So obviously the case is for רבי יהושע, and it teaches that the offering is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer, which said that פסולה refers only to lost or burned leftovers. It argues that the impure case must reflect רבי יהושע's view, and the משנה calls it פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, impure leftovers are an easier case than lost or burned leftovers, because at least they still exist. So the impure case teaches nothing new for him. It must have been stated for רבי יהושע, and that brings back the original question: why doesn't the ציץ help?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so there was no need to say it
Is it even necessary to say?
Lost or burned, meaning the part no longer exists
They are not there / it is still there

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Lost or burned means the leftovers are completely gone. Impure means they are still there but unfit. For רבי אליעזר, "gone" is the harder case, so "impure" goes without saying.

phrases.english: But "became impure" — according to whom does it teach it?
According to Rabbi Eliezer, it is obvious

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר אָבוּד וְשָׂרוּף דְּלֵיתַנְהוּ,
phrases.english: Now, where one can say they were lost or burned and are not there at all
Rabbi Eliezer declares it valid
Impure, where it still exists — is it even necessary to say?
Rather, it is obviously according to Rabbi Yehoshua
and it teaches that it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 24's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 24's claim that פסולה refers only to lost or burned leftovers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the impure case is pointless for רבי אליעזר, so it must teach רבי יהושע's view, and it says פסולה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהושע holds the frontplate does not cover the parts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when both the meat and the fat are impure, רבי יהושע does not allow sprinkling the blood. So he holds the ציץ does not atone for the burned or eaten parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהושע says: for all animal offerings in the תורה, whether the meat became impure and the fat is still fine, or the fat became impure and the meat is still fine, one sprinkles the blood. But if both became impure, one does not. So רבי יהושע must hold that the ציץ does not atone for the parts burned on the מזבח, nor for the parts that are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second attack, this time against step 22's answer. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהושע forbids sprinkling the blood when both parts are impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the ציץ covers impurity of both the burned parts and the eaten parts. If that were true, the blood could be sprinkled even when both are impure. Since the ברייתא forbids it, the ציץ apparently does not cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an additional challenge
The fat that is burned on the מזבח
He sprinkles the blood on the מזבח
The parts that go up (are burned) on the מזבח
The parts that are eaten
Evidently, introducing a conclusion drawn from a source

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says
All animal offerings in the Torah
whether the meat became impure and the fat remains
or the fat became impure and the meat remains
he sprinkles the blood.
But if both of them became impure — no.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is picking this up from how the ברייתא is worded.

phrases.english: Evidently Rabbi Yehoshua holds
the frontplate does not atone for the parts that go up on the altar
nor for the parts that are eaten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection, now aimed at step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 22's claim that, for רבי יהושע, the ציץ covers both the burned and the eaten parts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ציץ covered both parts, the blood could be sprinkled even when both are impure. The ברייתא forbids this.

steps.title: רבי יהושע is strict only before the fact
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the משנה does follow רבי יהושע. His rule of not sprinkling applies only לכתחילה. If it was already done (דיעבד), he accepts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה really does follow רבי יהושע, and there is no difficulty. One source speaks about what to do from the start, and the other speaks about after the fact. When רבי יהושע said not to sprinkle, he meant from the start. After the fact, he does not disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since both earlier answers were rejected, the גמרא gives a fresh answer. It splits רבי יהושע's view into two levels: what you should do from the start, and what counts if it was already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's "don't sprinkle" is only an instruction for how to act from the start. The משנה is discussing a case that already happened, and there רבי יהושע agrees the offering is accepted. So the two sources no longer contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth, returning to an earlier assumption
From the start, before acting
After the fact, once it was already done
Here... there, splitting two sources into different cases

steps.whatToRemember: New proposal: רבי יהושע's strictness is only לכתחילה, and דיעבד the offering works. Step 29 proves he makes this distinction, but Steps 30–31 reject using it to explain our משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: "Don't sprinkle" does not mean "if you sprinkled, it's invalid." לכתחילה rules and דיעבד rules can be different.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא מַתְנִיתִין,
phrases.english: Rather: actually, the Mishnah is Rabbi Yehoshua
and it is not difficult
Here — before the fact; there — after the fact.
When Rabbi Yehoshua spoke, it was about before the fact
after the fact — not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answers with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: לכתחילה vs. דיעבד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's "don't sprinkle" means the offering is invalid in all situations
steps.terutzMaskana: "Don't sprinkle" is only לכתחילה. דיעבד, the offering is accepted, which fits the משנה.

steps.title: Where do we see that רבי יהושע makes this distinction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that רבי יהושע distinguishes between לכתחילה and דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that רבי יהושע distinguishes between before the fact and after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for evidence for its new answer, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distinction in step 27 is not just a guess. The גמרא wants to show it is grounded in an explicit source about רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?
It makes a difference to him / he distinguishes

phrases.aramaic: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּשָׁנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: And from where do you say that Rabbi Yehoshua distinguishes
between before the fact and after the fact?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּשָׁנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for support for step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that רבי יהושע distinguishes between לכתחילה and דיעבד

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי יהושע agrees that if the blood was sprinkled, it is accepted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי יהושע says not to sprinkle the blood when the meat is impure or disqualified, yet he agrees that if it was sprinkled, the offering is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if the meat became impure, or became disqualified, or went outside the curtains of the courtyard, רבי אליעזר says the blood should be sprinkled. רבי יהושע says it should not be sprinkled. But רבי יהושע agrees that if someone did sprinkle it, the offering is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof it asked for. The ברייתא shows רבי יהושע saying "don't" from the start but "it counts" after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ומודה רבי יהושע ("and רבי יהושע agrees") show that his "don't sprinkle" was never a total disqualification. That is exactly the לכתחילה/דיעבד split from step 27, and it confirms the new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the curtains, meaning outside the permitted area
It (the blood) should be sprinkled
And he agrees / concedes
It is accepted (the offering achieves atonement)

steps.whatToRemember: ומודה רבי יהושע שאם זרק הורצה is the proof: רבי יהושע forbids only לכתחילה, and דיעבד the offering is accepted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proves that רבי יהושע distinguishes between לכתחילה and דיעבד. Even so, Steps 30–31 show this distinction does not fit the wording of the משניות, so it cannot explain our משנה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: if the meat became impure

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁנִּפְסַל אוֹ שֶׁיָּצָא חוּץ לַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: or it was disqualified, or it went outside the curtains
Rabbi Eliezer says: it should be sprinkled
Rabbi Yehoshua says: it should not be sprinkled.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁאִם זָרַק — הוּרְצָה.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua agrees that if he sprinkled it, it is accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28's request for a source
steps.raayaObject: Step 27's claim that רבי יהושע distinguishes between לכתחילה and דיעבד
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי יהושע says לא יזרק, yet concedes that if it was sprinkled, הורצה

steps.title: First reason: the word 'disqualified' means invalid even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about מנחות (Step 17) says the offering is ״פסולה״ according to רבי יהושע, and that word means invalid even בדיעבד. That clashes with the claim that רבי יהושע accepts the offering after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: One problem: the word 'disqualified' implies that it is invalid even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins rejecting the answer from step 27. Its first reason is that the word ״פסולה״, in the משנה about מנחות quoted in Step 17, does not sound like a mere 'don't do it at the start' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 27 said רבי יהושע forbids sprinkling the blood only לכתחילה but accepts it דיעבד. But the משנה about מנחות (Step 17) says that according to רבי יהושע the offering is ״פסולה״, which means truly invalid even after it was done. So רבי יהושע disqualifies even בדיעבד, which goes against the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: One (reason), opening a list of objections
Disqualified, invalid
After the fact, once it was already done
It implies, it indicates

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ״פסולה״ just means 'you shouldn't do it.' In this גמרא's reading, it means the offering doesn't work even if someone already did it.

phrases.english: One: that 'disqualified'
phrases.notes: The first of two objections, quoting the משנה's word

phrases.english: implies even after the fact.
phrases.notes: That is, invalid even once done, not just forbidden from the start

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תירוץ of step 27, which was supported in step 29, by showing that the משנה's wording does not fit it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהושע under a לכתחילה/דיעבד distinction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word ״פסולה״ means invalid even בדיעבד, so it cannot describe a rule that only restricts action לכתחילה.

steps.title: Second reason: 'five items are brought' describes doing it from the start
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's phrase ״חמשה דברים באין״ describes what may be brought לכתחילה. So the משנה is not speaking only about a דיעבד situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, 'five items are brought' implies that they may be brought from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason to reject the answer from step 27, again based on the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase ״באין״ means 'they are brought.' It describes a full permission to bring these offerings in טומאה from the outset. Step 27 needed the משנה to be talking only about accepting something after the fact, but the משנה clearly speaks in terms of לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an additional objection
Five items, the offerings the משנה says may be brought in טומאה
Are brought (offered)
From the start, before acting

steps.whatToRemember: The answer that the משנה follows רבי יהושע and only means 'don't do it at the start, but it works after the fact' is rejected. The משנה's words ״פסולה״ (invalid even after the fact) and ״באין״ (may be brought from the start) both point away from that split.

phrases.english: And furthermore, 'five items are brought'
phrases.notes: Quoting the opening of the משנה

phrases.english: implies from the start.
phrases.notes: The משנה is describing permission to bring them from the outset, not just after the fact

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent wording-based reason, alongside step 30, for rejecting the answer of step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes the rejection of the לכתחילה/דיעבד answer for the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ״באין״ describes a לכתחילה permission, while the answer required the משנה to describe only a דיעבד situation.
